what_this_is: The 0.2.1 REWIRING check, not a new result. In 0.2.0 the SparkInfer adapter drove the 0.1 CudaLocalityController directly, so TransitRuntime, TensorRegistry, TransitGraph, ITransitPlanner and CudaTransitExecutor were reachable only from the CLI and the tests: a contributor who wrote a planner changed nothing about the measured end-to-end number. 0.2.1 routes the adapter through TransitRuntime + CudaTransitExecutor and keeps the 0.1 controller as a second engine selected by TENSORTRANSIT_ENGINE, so the two can be A/B'd in ONE process against ONE model load. This file is that A/B. It answers one question: did putting the new core in the measured path change what the recurrent policy does? It did not. Both engines are token-exact against a reproducible control, both attach 96 windows to captured graph nodes with zero capture invalidations, and their gains agree within their own noise floors -- and with the +0.13% at a 0.06% floor that 0.2.0 published for this arm. PARTIAL matrix by design (batch 1, 0.40 of the section 44 weight), so decide.py will not call it significant; that is correct and is the point of running it as a check rather than as a submission.

provenance.note: Both arms in one session on one box, interleaved pairs, one binary. The only variable between the two rows below is TENSORTRANSIT_ENGINE.

how_it_was_checked: token-exact greedy replay against a control replayed against itself three times first

windows_attached_to_node == 96 on both engines: 2 graph captures x 48 recurrent layers, one window per layer. A second window per layer -- which persisting both the matrix and the convolution state would give -- would read 192, so this count pins the delivered policy and not just its telemetry.
capture_invalidations == 0 on both: the node attachment did not break the runtime's graph
the two gains overlap inside their own noise floors
what_is_new_and_not_a_regression: the transit engine registers the paged KV cache: recurrent_tensors 48, kv_tensors 16. No adapter exposed KV before, so the specification's second proof track could not be measured at all -- not 'had not been', could not be.
a planner is now on the measured path: TENSORTRANSIT_PLANNER, TENSORTRANSIT_ADMISSION and TENSORTRANSIT_PRESET change the plan the executor applies to this binary.

note_on_scope: Do NOT quote either figure as a TensorTransit result. This is the recurrent_v0 policy family, whose weighted ceiling is 0.52% on this model and 1.94% on the best model found -- both below the 2.0% floor the 0.1 scorer used. See README and docs/MINING.md.
